hook: Content note: the article sits behind an adult-content warning and deals directly with self-harm, suicide, non-consensual drugging and an abusive relationship. SCP-8557 is a phenomenon in which fresh self-inflicted wounds turn into mouths that talk back, kindly. It is short, clinical and very sad, and the one-line epigraph at the top sets its tone.
whyItMatters:
The file takes a body-horror image and makes the horror emotional rather than visual. The mouths are not hostile; they are the most understanding presence in the subject's life, and that comfort is exactly what drives the harm.

It also lets the containment procedures carry moral weight. The Foundation's answer involves lying to patients about their diagnosis and operating on them without consent if needed, and the text states this without a word of justification.
thingsToNotice:
The description borrows the vocabulary of addiction: the mouths read each host's fears and unresolved grief, and the dependence they create is compared chemically to drug use. The quoted testimonies, including the phrase about pain that does not hurt, explain why people cut more once the mouths appear, and a footnote adds that sutured instances only go dormant while staying in the body.

The history section turns the phenomenon into a person. Akari Tanaka, 19, had lived with the mouths since childhood, feeding and naming them like pets, while her girlfriend Himari Akiyama pushed her to keep cutting so there would be more of them and sedated her for long stretches to be alone with them; a recovered diary held over 70 photos of Tanaka's wounds. By the surgery nearly half her skin was scarred, six months later she killed herself, and the closing lines note that the only mourners at her funeral were Foundation staff watching for posthumous effects.
